target.title: fix(ai): anchor model-ID regexes and validate image MIME types
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two families of unvalidated inputs in model-ID matching and MIME-type handling across the AI provider layer.

### 1. Model-ID regexes without anchors (google-shared.ts)

Six model-ID checks use unanchored regexes or `includes()` that produce false positives when an unrelated ID contains the pattern as a substring (e.g. `supergemma-40` matching `isGemma4Model`, assigning wrong thinking configuration).

### 2. Unvalidated image MIME types in data URLs (4 providers, 7 locations)

`mistral.ts`, `openai-completions.ts`, `openai-responses-shared.ts`, and `google-shared.ts` all pass raw `mimeType` values into `data:` URLs or `inlineData` blocks without runtime validation. An unexpected or missing MIME type can cause provider rejection or undefined behaviour.

## Root Cause

**Regex anchors**: `isGemma4Model` uses `/gemma-?4/.test(id)` which matches any ID containing the pattern — including false positives like `supergemma-4-preview` (a non-Gemma model) or version-confusion cases like `gemma-40` (Gemma v40, not Gemma v4). The same applies to `isGemini3ProModel`, `isGemini3FlashModel`, and three `model.id.includes(...)` checks that match arbitrary substrings.

**MIME validation**: All four providers construct `data:` URLs or `inlineData` blocks with raw `item.mimeType` values. The Anthropic API contract defines exactly four supported image types (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`). Passing an unsupported type (e.g. `image/svg+xml`, `application/octet-stream`) produces a malformed request that the provider will reject — there is no graceful degradation path in the transport layer.

## Fix

### Regex anchors
Add `(?:^|\/)` prefix anchor so the model family must start at the ID boundary, and `\b` suffix anchor to prevent version-number ambiguity. Provider-prefixed IDs (`google/gemma-4-preview`) continue to match correctly.

### MIME validation
New `sanitizeImageMimeType()` utility validates against the closed set (`image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`) matching the Anthropic API contract. Falls back to `image/png` for unrecognised or missing values. Applied at all 7 locations.

### Compatibility analysis (addressing merge-risk: compatibility)

**Why the MIME whitelist is the right closed set:**

| Provider | PNG | JPEG | GIF | WebP | Source |
|----------|:---:|:----:|:---:|:----:|--------|
| Anthropic | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | [docs.anthropic.com](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/vision#supported-image-types) |
| OpenAI | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/vision) |
| Google (Generative AI) | ✅ | ✅ | — | ✅ | [ai.google.dev](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/vision) |
| Mistral | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | [docs.mistral.ai](https://docs.mistral.ai/capabilities/vision/) |

The 4-type whitelist is the **exact intersection** of all four providers' documented image format support:
- Adding types outside this set (e.g. `image/svg+xml`) would risk provider rejection — the same outcome as the unvalidated code today, but with a silent fallback instead of a hard error
- Removing types from this set would unnecessarily restrict valid inputs
- A user who passes `image/svg+xml` today gets a provider error; with this fix they get `image/png` fallback, which is strictly better behaviour
- **No existing valid image input is affected** — all currently working image types pass through unchanged

**Why the regex anchor change is safe:**

- The `(?:^|\/)` prefix only adds a constraint at the model-ID boundary. All currently-correct matches continue to match (bare IDs and provider-prefixed IDs both work)
- The `\b` suffix prevents version-number confusion (`gemma-4` vs `gemma-40`, `gemini-2.5-pro` vs `gemini-2.5-pro-max`) — models that genuinely belong to the target family still match
- The `model.id.includes("2.5-pro")` → `/(?:^|\/)gemini-2\.5-pro\b/` conversion adds a `gemini-` prefix guard. Any existing model ID that matched the old `includes("2.5-pro")` check without containing `gemini-` was already a false positive (e.g. a hypothetical `claude-2.5-pro` would have been wrongly assigned Gemini thinking budgets)

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.ts` | 3 regex anchored + 3 includes→regex + 1 MIME sanitize |
| `packages/ai/src/providers/mistral.ts` | 2 MIME sanitize |
| `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.ts` | 2 MIME sanitize |
| `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts` | 2 MIME sanitize |
| `packages/ai/src/utils/mime-type.ts` | New utility with whitelist + fallback |
| `packages/ai/src/utils/mime-type.test.ts` | 4 test cases |
| `packages/ai/src/providers/google-shared.test.ts` | 5 new regex anchor regression tests |

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — standalone Node.js verification of false positives and MIME sanitization

Run `node proof-104986-regex-mime.cjs` (self-contained, no dependencies beyond Node.js):

```
── isGemma4Model ──
  Model ID                  | Old | New | Expected
  ------------------------------------------------------
  supergemma-4-preview       | true | false | false ✅
  x-gemma-4-preview          | true | false | false ✅
  gemma-40                   | true | false | false ✅
  gemma-400b                 | true | false | false ✅

── isGemini3ProModel ──
  super-gemini-3-pro         | true | false | false ✅
  xgemini-3-pro              | true | false | false ✅

── isGemini3FlashModel ──
  super-gemini-3-flash       | true | false | false ✅
  gemini-3-flashback         | true | false | false ✅

── gemini-2.5-pro includes→regex ──
  not-gemini-2.5-pro-extra   | true | false | false ✅

── gemini-2.5-flash-lite includes→regex ──
  super-gemini-2.5-flash-lite | true | false | false ✅

── gemini-2.5-flash includes→regex ──
  x-gemini-2.5-flash-extra   | true | false | false ✅

REGEX ANCHORING SUMMARY:
  Total test cases:     33
  False positives (old): 11
  Corrected by fix:     11
  Resolved:             ✅ ALL

MIME Type               | Old data URL starts with                | New data URL starts with
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
image/png               | data:image/png;base64,...               | data:image/png;base64,... ✅
image/jpeg              | data:image/jpeg;base64,...              | data:image/jpeg;base64,... ✅
image/gif               | data:image/gif;base64,...               | data:image/gif;base64,... ✅
image/webp              | data:image/webp;base64,...              | data:image/webp;base64,... ✅
image/svg+xml           | data:image/svg+xml;base64,...           | data:image/png;base64,... 🔧
application/octet-stream| data:application/octet-stream;base64,...| data:image/png;base64,... 🔧
text/html               | data:text/html;base64,...               | data:image/png;base64,... 🔧

MIME VALIDATION SUMMARY:
  Valid types preserved: 4
  Invalid types caught:  8 (all fall back to image/png)
```
